A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Clarity framework and empirical study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original CUB and SUN experiments and a 50-participant human study, including classification, concept-quality, and trust results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and human-study outcomes, and adds regression, optimization-sensitivity, and repeated-seed findings in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The predictor/VLM formulations, amortized sparsity mechanisms, losses, classifier retraining, and inference procedures remain the same. V3 revises matrix notation and compresses the explanation, while relocating existing regularization details to Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CUB bird classification, SUN scene classification, and the same CUB-based human trust task. Generative multimodal concept detectors are newly discussed only as future work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same predictor/VLM, sparsity-method, Standard-CBM, Post-Hoc CBM, Label-Free CBM, Sparse-CBM, and Top-K comparators. V3 changes baseline tuning and reported outcomes, without adding or removing comparison methods.

E3.justification: V3 adds Post-Hoc regularization sweeps and Label-Free projection/SAGA budgets of 1000 versus 5000 steps, beyond v2's defaults-only description. Section 4 also reports validation-based threshold selection on a uniform 0.05 grid, but Appendix B retains v2's nonuniform threshold list; their relationship is unresolved.

E4.justification: V3 adds a regression testing whether Clarity predicts trust after controlling for sparsity, and targeted checks of baseline sensitivity to regularization and optimization depth. These extend the existing metric-weight sensitivity analysis, Top-K investigation, and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Appendix B first reports five independent seed runs for CUB VLM-based Bernoulli models with both backbones, including standard deviations for four metrics. V3 also adds regression coefficient tests, adjusted R-squared, and collinearity diagnostics. V2 already reported human-study uncertainty, but supplied no corresponding model-run count.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces Label-Free CBM's Clarity/accuracy/precision of 0.0020/74.14/0.0006 with 0.3540/70.10/0.1690, changing it from the lowest- to highest-Clarity global baseline. Its four Table 8 rows also change substantially. These revised results accompany expanded tuning, not a demonstrated same-setting gain. Regression and seed-variability outcomes are added; the main sparsity-method results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Clarity's harmonic-mean formulation and stated properties, along with the sparsity objectives and relaxations, are retained. V3 adds explanatory formulas for existing metric components and fixes notation; moving background mathematics and penalties to Appendix A does not introduce new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list recast Clarity as a post-hoc diagnostic of the flexibility-interpretability trade-off rather than a general principled measure of interpretability. The empirical contribution is explicitly restricted to the considered settings. The central trade-off, amortized-method, and trust-alignment claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies global-baseline conclusions by acknowledging their intended larger-vocabulary operating regimes. It expands the rationale against Pareto-based evaluation, interprets the regression as trust alignment beyond sparsity, and discusses unevaluated generative concept detectors and possible hallucination. The principal semantic-misalignment interpretation is retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-availability link, explicit instance averaging and zero precision for examples with no active concepts, threshold-selection documentation, and baseline hyperparameter ranges. Core hardware, optimizer, backbone, temperature, prior, and training-budget information was already present. These disclosures do not establish changes to every retained experiment.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens the research positioning through an attribute-based zero-shot-learning lineage, covering DAP, ALE, unreliable attributes, and semantic-preserving approaches. It explicitly connects modern CBM semantic drift to longstanding attribute-recognition problems. New foundation-model and generative-detector references further extend the previously CBM-focused discussion.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the exposition: the full sparse-representation background and detailed penalties move to Appendix A/A.1, the amortized-method explanation is compressed and rewritten, and the metric explanation becomes an explicit component-by-component account. Appendix organization, affiliations, publication text, and bibliographic wording are also revised.

P2.justification: All seven figures and eight tables are retained, with unchanged figure content and table structures. Publication headers and text reflow alter placement, including moving Table 2 from page 11 to page 10. The numerical replacements in Tables 4 and 8 are result changes rather than redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens comparison credibility through convergence checks and revised Label-Free CBM results, while improving metric documentation, research positioning, and statistical support. Its diagnostic framing and vocabulary caveat better qualify the conclusions. The gains remain limited: threshold descriptions in Section 4 and Appendix B are unreconciled, and calling Clarity the sole meaningful driver of trust overstates what the regression controlling only sparsity establishes.
